name: Ahmadzai Abdul Ghafoor
bio: Ahmadzai Abdul Ghafoor served on the security detail of Afghanistan's U.S.-backed president before entering the United States after the Taliban takeover. Immigration authorities detained him on May 30, 2025 under a suspected-terrorist designation, but did not produce evidence supporting that label in court; a federal judge granted habeas relief and ordered his release on May 13, 2026 after nearly a year in custody.
sources: Court Watch report on the habeas ruling

case.charges: Immigration detention based on a government suspected-terrorist designation that was not substantiated in the habeas proceeding.
case.sentence: Civil immigration detention; release ordered on habeas review.

name: Douglas Thrams
bio: Douglas Thrams was prosecuted over TikTok videos that advocated attacks on President Donald Trump, Elon Musk, government buildings, and other political targets. Arrested on January 24, 2025, he pleaded guilty to interstate threats and received a time-served sentence after serving ten months and fourteen days.
sources: Court Watch report on the threat prosecution

case.charges: Making interstate threats through political videos posted to TikTok.
case.sentence: Time served after ten months and fourteen days in custody.

name: Tyler Miles Leveque
bio: Tyler Miles Leveque was arrested after online posts threatening President Donald Trump, Elon Musk, corporate executives, and state offices. He pleaded guilty to transmitting threats in interstate commerce and, on December 3, 2025, received a sentence approximating the ten months he had already spent in custody plus three years of supervision.
sources: Court Watch report on the arrest

case.charges: Transmitting interstate threats against political and corporate targets.
case.convicted: Yes — transmitting threats in interstate commerce.
case.sentence: Approximately ten months in custody followed by three years of supervised release.

name: Alexander Justin White
bio: Alexander Justin White was arrested on December 4, 2024 after federal agents alleged that he tried to travel abroad to join ISIS and promoted the organization online. He pleaded guilty to conspiring and attempting to provide material support and was sentenced on June 22, 2026 to eight years in federal prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the case

case.charges: Conspiracy and attempt to provide material support to ISIS.
case.convicted: Yes — conspiracy and attempt to provide material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization.

name: Gunner Joseph Fisher
bio: Gunner Joseph Fisher was arrested in December 2024 after authorities alleged that he planned a mass shooting at a Nashville mosque and invoked the Christchurch attacks. He later received a 24-month federal sentence; public reporting says the prison term began in July 2026.
sources: Court Watch report on the alleged mosque plot

case.charges: Federal offenses arising from an alleged plan to attack a Nashville mosque.

name: Forrest Kendall Pemberton
bio: Forrest Kendall Pemberton is a Florida defendant accused of traveling to South Florida with firearms while planning an attack on employees of the American Israel Public Affairs Committee. Arrested in late December 2024, he remains charged in a federal case; the allegations have not been proved at trial.

case.charges: Attempted mass shooting targeting Jewish victims and related firearms offenses.
case.indicted: Yes — federally indicted; a later indictment was announced June 18, 2026.

name: Brad Kenneth Spafford
bio: Brad Kenneth Spafford was arrested on December 17, 2024 after investigators found more than 150 homemade explosive devices at his Virginia property. Prosecutors cited anti-government views and statements about political assassination; he was convicted of explosives and firearms offenses and sentenced on December 18, 2025 to eight years in prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the explosives seizure

case.charges: Possession of unregistered destructive devices and a firearm while an unlawful user of a controlled substance.
case.convicted: Yes — federal explosives and firearms offenses.

name: Brian J. Cole Jr.
bio: Brian J. Cole Jr. is the man federal prosecutors accuse of placing pipe bombs outside the Republican and Democratic national headquarters on January 5, 2021. He was arrested on December 4, 2025 and later indicted; the charges remain allegations while the federal case is pending.
sources: Court Watch review of the court record

case.charges: Transporting and attempting to use explosive devices outside the Republican and Democratic national headquarters.

name: Abdullah Ezzeldin Taha Mohamed Hassan
bio: Abdullah Ezzeldin Taha Mohamed Hassan was arrested on December 16, 2024 after an FBI operation in which an informant said Hassan directed plans for an attack on the Israeli consulate in New York in the name of ISIS. A court ordered him detained pending trial; the accusations remain unproved.
sources: Court Watch report on the case

case.charges: Distribution of information relating to explosives and alleged direction of an ISIS-inspired attack plot.

name: Rene Ortiz
bio: Rene Ortiz was arrested on January 17, 2025 after delivering written threats to federal courthouses that called for the killing of whichever candidate won the 2024 presidential election. A jury convicted him on June 8, 2026 of threatening President Donald Trump and former Vice President Kamala Harris; the latest confirmed public source reviewed for this import did not establish his final sentence.
sources: Court Watch report on the charging papers

case.charges: Threats against the president, successors to the presidency, and a former president.
case.convicted: Yes — convicted by a federal jury on June 8, 2026.
case.sentence: Final sentencing disposition not established in the sources reviewed.

name: Reda Mazen Rida Sabassi
bio: Reda Mazen Rida Sabassi was arrested on June 16, 2026 on charges that he used purported Gaza relief fundraising to finance Hamas. The federal case is pending and the government's allegations have not been proved at trial.
sources: Court Watch report, Holy Land Foundation Redux

case.charges: Conspiracy to provide material support to Hamas through alleged fundraising transfers.

name: Raed Yousef
bio: Raed Yousef is a Florida defendant accused of funneling money to Hamas. A federal court ordered him detained pending trial on September 23, 2026; the charges remain allegations and no conviction has been established.
sources: Court Watch report, Holy Land Foundation Redux

case.charges: Providing or conspiring to provide material support to Hamas.

name: Mahmoud Amin Ya'qub Al-Muhtadi
affiliation: Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine
bio: Mahmoud Amin Ya'qub Al-Muhtadi was arrested in Louisiana on October 16, 2025 on allegations that he participated in the October 7, 2023 attack in Israel and concealed that conduct in a U.S. visa application. His federal case remains pending and the allegations have not been proved at trial.
sources: Court Watch report, Holy Land Foundation Redux

case.charges: Providing material support to a foreign terrorist organization and visa fraud arising from alleged participation in the October 7 attack.

name: Tina Peters
bio: Tina Peters, the former Mesa County clerk, was convicted in Colorado of crimes arising from a breach of county election equipment carried out while she promoted claims of election fraud. On October 3, 2024 she was sentenced to nine years of incarceration; a later federal pardon did not reach her state convictions.
sources: Court Watch report on the state conviction and federal pardon issue

case.charges: Attempting to influence a public servant, conspiracy to commit criminal impersonation, official misconduct, and related state offenses arising from an election-system breach.

name: Nasir Ahmad Tawhedi
bio: Nasir Ahmad Tawhedi was arrested on October 7, 2024 after an undercover operation in which prosecutors said he planned an ISIS-inspired attack on Election Day. He pleaded guilty and was sentenced to fifteen years in federal prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the case

case.charges: Conspiracy and attempt to provide material support to ISIS and firearms offenses tied to an alleged Election Day attack plan.

name: Zimnako Salah
bio: Zimnako Salah was arrested on November 28, 2023 after federal investigators alleged that he repeatedly placed backpacks at Christian churches while researching explosives and attacks. A jury convicted him of attempting to provide material support to ISIS and he was sentenced on November 7, 2025 to six years in prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the prosecution

case.charges: Attempting to provide material support to ISIS and making a false statement to federal agents.
case.convicted: Yes — convicted by a federal jury.

name: Ahmad Khalil Elshazly
bio: Ahmad Khalil Elshazly was arrested on December 15, 2019 after an FBI operation concerning his plan to travel to Syria and fight for ISIS. He pleaded guilty to attempting to provide material support and, on September 28, 2026, received a 92-month federal sentence.
sources: Court Watch report on the case

case.charges: Attempting to provide material support to ISIS through planned travel to Syria.
case.convicted: Yes — attempting to provide material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization.

name: Gokhan Gun
bio: Gokhan Gun, a civilian Defense Department engineer with a top-secret clearance, was arrested on August 9, 2024 after agents found classified documents at his home as he prepared to travel to Mexico. He pleaded guilty to unauthorized removal and retention of classified material and was sentenced on June 17, 2025 to eighteen months in prison, three years of supervision, and a $25,000 fine.
sources: Court Watch report on the case
Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency case study

case.charges: Unauthorized removal and retention of classified material.
case.convicted: Yes — unauthorized removal and retention of classified material.
case.sentence: Eighteen months in prison, three years of supervised release, and a $25,000 fine.

name: Hadi Matar
bio: Hadi Matar was arrested on August 12, 2022 after stabbing author Salman Rushdie onstage at the Chautauqua Institution. A New York jury convicted him of attempted murder and assault, and he received a 25-year state sentence in May 2025; a parallel federal terrorism prosecution followed.
sources: Court Watch report on the state and federal proceedings

case.charges: Attempted murder and assault in state court, with parallel federal terrorism-related charges.
case.convicted: Yes — attempted murder and assault in New York state court.
case.sentence: Twenty-five years in state prison; parallel federal proceedings followed.

name: Abdulrahman Mohammed Hafedh Alqaysi
bio: Abdulrahman Mohammed Hafedh Alqaysi, an Iraqi refugee and lawful permanent resident, admitted providing technical and media assistance to ISIS between 2015 and 2020. In federal custody since June 16, 2022, he pleaded guilty and was sentenced on October 9, 2025 to twelve years in prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the case

case.charges: Providing material support to ISIS and related fraud, identity-theft, and immigration offenses.
case.sentence: Twelve years in federal prison followed by three years of supervised release.

name: Samir Ousman Alsheikh
bio: Samir Ousman Alsheikh, a former director of Syria's Adra Prison and provincial governor under Bashar al-Assad, was arrested at Los Angeles International Airport on July 10, 2024. A federal jury convicted him of torture, conspiracy, and immigration fraud for abuses used to punish political dissent, and on September 17, 2026 he was sentenced to sixty years in prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the prosecution

case.charges: Conspiracy to commit torture, torture, immigration-document fraud, and attempted naturalization fraud.
case.convicted: Yes — convicted on all six federal counts.

name: Nathan Vilas Laatsch
bio: Nathan Vilas Laatsch, a former Defense Intelligence Agency employee, was arrested on May 29, 2025 after giving classified documents to an undercover FBI agent he believed represented a foreign government. He pleaded guilty in August 2026 to transmitting national-defense information and remained in custody awaiting a January 2027 sentencing.
sources: Court Watch report, Charity for Hamas

case.charges: Transmission of national-defense information to a person believed to represent a foreign government.

name: Sinmyah Amera Ceasar
bio: Sinmyah Amera Ceasar pleaded guilty in 2017 to recruiting for ISIS, then admitted obstructing justice and fleeing while on release. She was returned to federal custody after a two-day flight in 2021 and, on April 9, 2025, was resentenced across the three cases to 230 months in prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the prosecution

case.charges: Conspiracy to provide material support to ISIS, obstruction of justice, and failure to appear.
case.plead: Guilty in three separately charged cases.
case.sentence: Two hundred thirty months in federal prison.

name: Dallas Humber
bio: Dallas Humber led the Terrorgram Collective, a white-supremacist network that promoted political murder, hate crimes, and attacks on critical infrastructure. Arrested on September 6, 2024, she pleaded guilty and was sentenced on December 17, 2025 to thirty years in federal prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the case

case.charges: Soliciting hate crimes, soliciting the murder of federal officials, and conspiring to provide material support to terrorists.
case.sentence: Thirty years in federal prison and lifetime supervised release.

name: Awais Chudhary
bio: Awais Chudhary was arrested on August 29, 2019 during an FBI operation concerning plans for an ISIS-inspired knife attack in Queens. He pleaded guilty to attempting to provide material support and was sentenced on September 23, 2025 to nine years in federal prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the case

case.charges: Attempting to provide material support to ISIS through preparation for an attack in Queens.
case.sentence: Nine years in federal prison followed by fifteen years of supervised release.

name: Mohammed Azharuddin Chhipa
bio: Mohammed Azharuddin Chhipa raised and converted money to cryptocurrency that prosecutors said supported ISIS fighters and helped women escape detention camps in Syria. Arrested on May 4, 2023, he was convicted at trial and sentenced on May 7, 2025 to 364 months in federal prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the case

case.charges: Conspiracy and substantive counts of providing or attempting to provide material support to ISIS.
case.convicted: Yes — convicted by a federal jury.
case.sentence: Three hundred sixty-four months in federal prison.

name: Benjamin Hanil Song
bio: Benjamin Hanil Song was arrested after the July 4, 2025 armed attack on the Prairieland ICE Detention Center in Alvarado, Texas, which prosecutors characterized as an Antifa cell operation. He was convicted of terrorism and related offenses and sentenced on June 23, 2026 to one hundred years in federal prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the North Texas prosecution

case.charges: Attempted murder of federal officers, terrorism, firearms, and related offenses arising from the Prairieland ICE facility attack.
case.sentence: One hundred years in federal prison.

name: Bradford Morris
bio: Bradford Morris was arrested in connection with the July 4, 2025 armed attack on the Prairieland ICE Detention Center in Alvarado, Texas, which prosecutors characterized as an Antifa cell operation. He was convicted and sentenced on June 23, 2026 to fifty years in federal prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the North Texas prosecution

case.charges: Terrorism, firearms, and related offenses arising from the Prairieland ICE facility attack.

name: Daniel Rolando Sanchez-Estrada
bio: Daniel Rolando Sanchez-Estrada was arrested in connection with the July 4, 2025 armed attack on the Prairieland ICE Detention Center in Alvarado, Texas, which prosecutors characterized as an Antifa cell operation. He was convicted and sentenced on June 23, 2026 to thirty years in federal prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the North Texas prosecution

case.charges: Terrorism, firearms, and related offenses arising from the Prairieland ICE facility attack.

name: Regan Darby Prater
bio: Regan Darby Prater is accused of setting fire to the Highlander Research and Education Center, a historic civil-rights and labor-education institution, while invoking neo-Nazi ideas. He was ordered held after a May 8, 2025 court appearance; the federal arson and explosives charges remain pending.
sources: Court Watch report on the filing

case.charges: Arson and explosives offenses arising from the fire at the Highlander Research and Education Center.

name: Catherine Beth Washburn
bio: Catherine Beth Washburn, an upstate New York Palestine activist, was arrested on June 30, 2026 on allegations that she attempted to provide material support to Palestinian Islamic Jihad. Her federal case is pending and the allegations have not been proved at trial.
sources: Court Watch report on the case

case.charges: Attempting to provide material support to Palestinian Islamic Jihad.

name: Michael Sam Teekaye Jr.
bio: Michael Sam Teekaye Jr. was arrested at Baltimore-Washington International Airport on October 14, 2024 after investigators said he intended to travel abroad to join ISIS and had discussed attacking Jewish and Israeli targets if he could not leave. He pleaded guilty and was sentenced on July 8, 2026 to fifteen years in federal prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the case

case.charges: Attempting to provide material support to ISIS.
case.sentence: Fifteen years in federal prison followed by lifetime supervised release.

name: Aws Mohammed Naser
bio: Aws Mohammed Naser was federally indicted in 2022 while serving state custody connected to a 2017 destructive-device case. A jury convicted him of attempting to provide material support to ISIS and possessing a destructive device, and on May 7, 2026 he was sentenced to twenty years in federal prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the case

case.charges: Attempting to provide material support to ISIS and possessing a destructive device as a felon.
case.convicted: Yes — convicted by a federal jury.

name: Stefan Day Rowold
bio: Stefan Day Rowold was arrested on July 8, 2024 after twice breaking into, vandalizing, and setting fires inside a Latter-day Saints church in Wiggins, Mississippi because of his hostility to the church's religious views. A federal jury convicted him of arson and civil-rights offenses, and he was sentenced in February 2026 to thirty years in prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the case

case.charges: Federal arson and civil-rights offenses for attacking a house of worship because of its religious character.
case.convicted: Yes — convicted by a federal jury on six counts.

name: Clift Seferlis
bio: Clift Seferlis mailed dozens of threatening letters and postcards to Jewish institutions, many referring to Israel, Gaza, or violence against Jewish people. Arrested on June 16, 2025, he pleaded guilty to mailing threats and obstructing religious exercise and was sentenced on March 16, 2026 to thirty-seven months in federal prison.
sources: Court Watch report on the case

case.charges: Mailing threatening communications and obstructing the free exercise of religious beliefs.
case.sentence: Thirty-seven months in federal prison, three years of supervised release, and a $40,000 fine.

name: Michael Ron David Kadar
bio: Michael Ron David Kadar, a U.S.-Israeli citizen, was extradited from Norway and arraigned in Florida on June 22, 2026 on allegations that he made threats against Jewish institutions, the Israeli embassy, and the Anti-Defamation League. The federal cases remain pending and the accusations have not been proved at trial.
sources: Court Watch report, Holy Land Foundation Redux
Justice Department extradition and arraignment release

case.charges: Interstate and international threats against Jewish institutions and organizations in several federal districts.
